title: The Great Molasses Flood — जब बोस्टन की सड़कों पर शीरे की लहर दौड़ी

lines.text: 15 जनवरी 1919 की दोपहर। बोस्टन का नॉर्थ एंड, कमर्शियल स्ट्रीट।
lines.spoken: पंद्रह जनवरी उन्नीस सौ उन्नीस की दोपहर। बोस्टन का नॉर्थ एंड, कमर्शियल स्ट्रीट।

lines.text: एक विशाल टैंक से तेईस लाख गैलन शीरा सड़कों पर बह निकला।

lines.text: अगले दिन के बोस्टन पोस्ट ने लिखा कि लहर 50 फ़ुट ऊँची थी; यह आँकड़ा विवादित है।

lines.visual: the Post headline '11 DEAD, 50 HURT' underlined

lines.text: मीठा, गाढ़ा शीरा। वह किसी की जान कैसे ले सकता है?

lines.text: जवाब उसी समय के एक अख़बार में है, और लगभग एक सदी बाद लिखे शहर के विवरण में।

lines.text: शहर के मुताबिक़, यह 50 फ़ुट ऊँचा था और इसमें लगभग तेईस लाख गैलन शीरा भरा जा सकता था।

fact_notes: C1: On the afternoon of January 15, 1919, a giant tank released 2,300,000 gallons of molasses over Commercial Street in Boston's North End. [S1: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Boston_post-January_16,_1919,.jpg]
C2: The wave swept Commercial Street and its waterfront from Charter Street to the southern end of North End Park. [S1: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Boston_post-January_16,_1919,.jpg]

C3: The flood caught more than 100 men, women and children, and crushed buildings, horse teams, automobiles and street cars. [S1: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Boston_post-January_16,_1919,.jpg]
C4: The mass struck the buildings facing Copp's Hill and then swept back towards the harbour. [S1: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Boston_post-January_16,_1919,.jpg]
C5: By midnight the next day's paper counted eleven known dead, a woman, a girl and nine men, and more than 50 injured. [S1: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Boston_post-January_16,_1919,.jpg]

C6: The final toll was 21 dead and about 150 injured. [S6: https://www.boston.gov/news/100-years-ago-today-molasses-crashes-through-bostons-north-end; S2: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Molasses_Flood; S4: https://www.npr.org/2019/01/13/684894921/after-100-years-a-look-back-at-bostons-great-molasses-flood-of-1919; S3: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Great-Molasses-Flood]

C7: How high the wave was is disputed: the Boston Post reported 50 feet; later accounts give figures from about 15 to 40 feet, most often 25 feet. [S1: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Boston_post-January_16,_1919,.jpg; S2: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Molasses_Flood; S4: https://www.npr.org/2019/01/13/684894921/after-100-years-a-look-back-at-bostons-great-molasses-flood-of-1919; S3: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Great-Molasses-Flood]

C8: The wave is estimated to have moved at about 35 miles an hour. [S6: https://www.boston.gov/news/100-years-ago-today-molasses-crashes-through-bostons-north-end; S2: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Molasses_Flood; S11: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:BostonMolassesDisaster.jpg]
C9: The elevated railway structure on Commercial Street was crushed. [S1: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Boston_post-January_16,_1919,.jpg]
C10: Among the dead was George Lahey (as the Post spells it), an engineer of Engine 31 of the Boston Fire Department. [S1: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Boston_post-January_16,_1919,.jpg]
C11: Among the unidentified dead was a girl of about 14 with an employment tag from the Revere Rubber Company. [S1: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Boston_post-January_16,_1919,.jpg]
C12: Dead horses, cats and dogs were carted away, and Boston's only trolley freight terminal was in ruins. [S1: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Boston_post-January_16,_1919,.jpg]
C13: Ambulances were rushed from all over the city, and rescuers worked on the North End Park playground. [S1: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Boston_post-January_16,_1919,.jpg]

C14: The day after, a state police chemist, W. L. Wedger, concluded that an internal explosion, not a collapse, had caused the disaster; this first explanation did not stand. [S1: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Boston_post-January_16,_1919,.jpg]
C15: On January 15, 1919, 35 states had ratified the Prohibition amendment and one more was needed. [S1: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Boston_post-January_16,_1919,.jpg]

C25: The tank, 50 feet tall and holding about 2.3 million gallons, was built in 1915 by the Purity Distilling Company. [S6: https://www.boston.gov/news/100-years-ago-today-molasses-crashes-through-bostons-north-end]
C26: The tank had reportedly leaked before the disaster. [S6: https://www.boston.gov/news/100-years-ago-today-molasses-crashes-through-bostons-north-end]

C27: Structural engineers later found the tank's walls too thin and its material vulnerable to cracking. [S6: https://www.boston.gov/news/100-years-ago-today-molasses-crashes-through-bostons-north-end]

C28: Poor construction, changes in temperature and a large shipment of molasses together contributed to the rupture. [S6: https://www.boston.gov/news/100-years-ago-today-molasses-crashes-through-bostons-north-end]

C29: In 1925 a court-appointed auditor attributed the disaster to negligence by the tank's owners. [S6: https://www.boston.gov/news/100-years-ago-today-molasses-crashes-through-bostons-north-end; S5: https://www.history.com/news/the-great-molasses-flood-of-1919; S7: https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/state-house-tours/did-you-know/Molasses-Flood.htm]
